newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk sale may produce scandal -minister.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk sale may produce scandal -minister.

text.p: Controversy surrounding Russia's recent Svyazinvest telecoms sale could affect the forthcoming auction of another Russian jewel, the Norilsk Nickel metals group, a senior property official said on Thursday.

Privatisation Minister Alfred Kokh was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying he did not exclude the possibility that the Norilsk sale could generate a similar scandal involving the reformist cabinet and media interests controlled by Russia's leading, politically-connected, commercial banks.
Bidding for a 38 percent stake in Norilsk, one of the world's largest nickel and precious metals producers, closes on Friday, with results due August 5.
Uneximbank, one of Russia's most powerful commercial banks, is tendering the Norilsk stake, which represents 51 percent of the voting shares.

Uneximbank also led the consortium of U.S. and German financial interests which won the Svyazinvest auction last week, which at $1.875 billion was Russia's largest privatisation to date. Observers expect the bank to win the Norilsk stake.

Russian media, widely controlled by domestic banks which placed a losing bid for Svyazinvest, plunged the government into near-crisis over the sale by attacking the Kremlin for awarding a prime company to one group instead of to another.

In terms of price, the Svyazinvest sale was widely viewed as fair in that it represented a decent market value for a major Russian company, something not often seen in Russia's sell off of major enterprises.
